subject: SkyTrail POC: technical commitments, success criteria & integration outline
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Gupta <aisha.gupta@skytrail.ai>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@skytrail.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T16:12:00Z
Subject: SkyTrail POC: technical commitments, success criteria & integration outline

Hi Aisha / Tom,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great discussion and clear business context on the entity-resolution feature you want to accelerate with an embedded LLM. Per our agreement, I’m capturing the immediate POC scope, success criteria, owners, and a proposed integration outline so everyone has a single source of truth. Please read the bullets below and flag anything missing.

High-level POC objective:
- Validate Redwood inference for near-real-time entity resolution across SkyTrail’s ingestion pipeline (avg latency target <= 250ms 95th pct for 512-token windows).

Success criteria (proposal):
- Functional: 95% match against SkyTrail golden set (50k labeled rows) for entity merge decisions.
- Performance: end-to-end P95 <= 250ms when using Redwood streaming + prefix cache with 8 concurrent streams.
- Cost: under $1.50 per 1k inference tokens on average for the trial period.
- Operability: reproducible eval script + simple rollback to smaller model variant if regressions seen.

POC timeline (target):
- Week 0 (kickoff): finalize MLP/MAP and access to test dataset (next business day).
- Week 1: Redwood to provide SDK sandbox, model variant suggestions, and sample integration endpoints.
- Week 2: SkyTrail integration of SDK + smoke tests using subset of data.
- Week 3: Run full evaluation, collect metrics, and review outcomes.

Owners & contacts:
- SkyTrail: Aisha (POC lead), Tom (platform)
- Redwood: Neha (deal lead), Marissa Cole (solutions/SE), Rishi Malhotra (integration engineer), Monica Patel (CS/backstop)

Integration outline (initial):
- SDK: Redwood SDK (Python + Node) embedded into your transform worker. Use the streaming generate() path for low latency.
- API routes: recommend /v1/generate-stream for inference, /v1/kv-cache for warm-starts when reusing prior contexts.
- Tokenization: use Redwood-tokenizer v2 for consistent token accounting; we’ll include a small script for your pipeline.
- Tool calling: if you plan to call downstream enrichment (fuzzy match service), implement idempotent callbacks using our tool-calling webhook pattern.

Attachments included: suggested success criteria doc and SDK quickstart (attached).

Next steps (actionable):
1) Aisha: confirm access to the 50k golden set and desired PII masking rules by EOD Tues 4/19.
2) Redwood (Marissa/Rishi): provision sandbox API keys and share the SDK link by Wed 4/20.
3) Both teams: schedule a 30-min tech-handoff on Thu 4/21 to walk integration details.

Thanks — I’ll open the MAP in HubSpot and post the Drive link.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

--

Thanks Neha — this is super helpful. Quick responses inline and a couple clarifying asks: 

- Dataset: we can expose a sanitized 50k set (PII masked) by EOD Tuesday 4/19. I’ll share S3 credentials with your team.
- Latency: 250ms P95 is aggressive but aligns with our UX goals. If the streaming path needs a small kernel/quantized variant to hit that, we’re open.
- Cost: our budget for the POC is $4k total, so the $1.50/1k target is a helpful input — can you confirm estimated spend for the 3-week trial based on our volume (~200k tokens/day)?

Integration asks:
- Can you share a short example of the streaming client usage inside a Python worker (we use Airflow to trigger transforms)?
- Are there any infra requirements for the KV-cache path (Redis vs in-memory vs Redwood-managed)?

We’d like the tech-handoff on Thu 4/21 10:00am PT if that works for your engineers.

Appreciate it — Aisha
Aisha Gupta

Neha / team / Aisha — quick update ahead of the handoff:

1) Sandbox keys & SDK: I’ve provisioned scoped sandbox keys for the streaming generate endpoint and uploaded the redwood-sdk-integration-guide.zip to the shared Drive folder (link in HubSpot MAP).

2) Streaming example (Python snippet):
- Use redwood.client.StreamingClient(api_key=...)
- Call client.generate_stream(model='rwd-pt-small', prompt=prompt, max_tokens=512)
- Consume async chunked iterator and commit KV-cache entries after each record for warm starts.

3) KV-cache options:
- Redwood-managed cache (recommended for POC): no infra changes, supports hot prefix caching and evictions.
- Self-hosted Redis: lower variance but requires you to maintain a small Redis cluster and configure our KV sync bridge.

4) Fallback plan: we’ll include an automatic model-variant policy (rwd-pt-small -> rwd-pt-quant) that kicks in on latency SLO breaches. RACI: Redwood impl, SkyTrail approves thresholds.

5) Cost estimate: based on ~200k tokens/day and our suggested config, estimated cost is ~$3,360 over the three-week POC (below your $4k cap). I’ll attach a simple cost calc in the Drive.

I’ll be on the tech-handoff call at 10:00am PT today to walk the snippet and go over runbook items.

-Rishi
